extracted.intended_audience: MIT researchers, faculty, staff and students who create inventions and may pursue commercialization
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for MIT inventors on the steps, expectations, and behaviors needed to disclose inventions, pursue patent protection, and license technologies through the MIT Technology Licensing Office (TLO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting a technology disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers disclose innovations to the TLO after they have demonstrated a new invention. This leads to the TLO's evaluation of the disclosure subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process begins with a disclosure submitted via the MIT Technology Disclosure in the Research@MIT app; disclosure triggers evaluation by the TLO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the TLO promptly when you suspect an invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting the TLO as soon as you believe you have a scientific or technical observation with potential commercial or research value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early contact helps preserve patent rights and allows the TLO to advise on next steps and disclosure timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient time to file a patent application before public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing sufficient time to file a patent application by completing and submitting the MIT Technology Disclosure in the Research@MIT app at least one month before submitting the manuscript for publication or before publicly disclosing your technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File disclosures well before manuscripts, presentations, or other public disclosures to avoid jeopardizing patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid external discussions before protection (unless NDA in place)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstaining from discussions with people outside the MIT community (other than under a nondisclosure agreement) to avoid risking MIT's ability to pursue patent protection on an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public or informal disclosures to external parties can destroy novelty; use an NDA if you must discuss externally prior to patent filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow MIT to negotiate NDAs with third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing MIT to negotiate a Non-Disclosure Agreement with any outside party in the event you need to discuss your invention with a third party prior to obtaining a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the TLO handle NDA terms to protect MIT's rights and ensure appropriate confidentiality language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share contact information for potentially interested parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing any company or personal contact information for those you believe may be interested in MIT intellectual property or who may have already contacted you about an MIT invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide leads and contacts to assist the TLO's commercialization and licensing outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a responsive partner during the patenting process
rubrics_metrics.description: Committing to being a responsive partner during the patent process—we strive to make efficient use of your time, but the patenting process does take several years, and there will be times when you are expected to respond to requests from the TLO and the outside patent counsel hired by MIT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses to information requests and collaboration with outside counsel are essential for effective prosecution and commercialization; expect multi-year timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the TLO informed of publications and company interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping the TLO informed of upcoming publications or interactions with companies related to your intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice of publications or meetings with companies lets the TLO coordinate patent filings or NDAs to protect rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: TLO evaluation and selective patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: The TLO evaluates the invention, selectively elects to protect inventions with patent protection, and explores commercialization avenues to bring the technology to market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every disclosure will receive patent protection; the TLO assesses commercial potential, patentability, and resource allocation when deciding whether to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization via licensing agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing agreements are negotiated, leading to the licensee's further development commercialization of the technology, generating revenue for both MIT and the inventor, which supports further research and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful tech transfer typically involves negotiating licenses (to established companies or startups) that fund further development and return revenue to MIT and inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to participate (motivations for inventors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential reasons may include: making a positive impact on society; feeling a sense of professional fulfillment; achieving recognition and financial reward; generating additional department/center funding; meeting the obligations of a research contract; attracting research sponsors; creating educational opportunities for students; linking students to future job opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These motivations can guide an inventor's engagement with the tech transfer process and help communicate value to collaborators and sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of technology transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Our new technology transferred to industry enhances industrial competitiveness, brings new products and services to the public, and fosters economic development and new jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also emphasizes institutional benefits: deepening company relationships, facilitating additional research projects, broader educational opportunities, and collaborative investments that support MIT's mission.
